questions.q: Why is gradient norm often considered an earlier warning signal than the loss curve itself?
options: Gradient norm is logged more frequently than loss
A gradient-norm spike can precede or coincide with a loss spike, and a gradual upward drift can indicate growing instability before loss visibly moves
Gradient norm is unrelated to training stability
Gradient norm only matters after training finishes
questions.explain: Because gradient norm reflects the raw update magnitude before clipping, it frequently shows trouble (a spike or a slow upward drift) before the effect becomes visible in the loss curve.

questions.q: What does held-out evaluation loss catch that training loss alone cannot reliably catch?
options: GPU hardware failures
Overfitting or data leakage, since evaluation loss is computed on data never used for training
Learning rate scheduler bugs
Tokenizer vocabulary errors
questions.explain: Evaluation loss is measured on held-out data the model never trained on, so a widening gap between training and evaluation loss can reveal overfitting or leakage that training loss by itself wouldn't show.

questions.q: What does Model FLOPs Utilization (MFU) measure?
options: The percentage of training data that has been processed so far
The fraction of a GPU's theoretical peak FLOPs actually being used for useful model computation
The number of model parameters relative to dataset size
The accuracy of the model on a benchmark
questions.explain: MFU is the ratio of actual achieved FLOPs to the GPU's theoretical peak FLOPs, measuring computational efficiency rather than model quality.

questions.q: A run's MFU suddenly drops while loss and gradient norm behave completely normally. What does this pattern most likely indicate?
options: The model has started overfitting
An infrastructure problem -- such as a slow node, data-loading bottleneck, or communication stall -- rather than anything about the model itself
The learning rate schedule has a bug
The dataset has run out of tokens
questions.explain: A drop in MFU with no corresponding change in loss or gradient norm typically points to an infrastructure or throughput issue rather than a problem with the model's learning dynamics.

questions.q: What role do tools like Weights & Biases or TensorBoard play in monitoring a pretraining run?
options: They replace the need for gradient clipping
They turn the stream of logged scalars (loss, gradient norm, learning rate, throughput) into live, shareable dashboards for real-time monitoring
They automatically fix loss spikes without human intervention
They are only used after training completes, never during
questions.explain: Experiment trackers collect per-step logged metrics and render them as live dashboards, letting a team watch loss, gradient norm, and throughput in real time rather than reading raw logs.
